s01.text: Most people assume GPS is simple geometry: satellites broadcast their location and your phone triangulates your position.

s02.text: In truth, if satellite engineers had relied on classical Newtonian physics, your navigation map would drift by over ten kilometers every single day.

s03.text: Because GPS satellites orbit at nearly four kilometers per second, Einstein's Special Relativity dictates their clocks tick slower, losing seven microseconds a day.

s04.text: However, twenty thousand kilometers above Earth, gravity is four times weaker, and General Relativity dictates that weaker gravity makes clocks run forty-five microseconds faster.

s05.text: Subtracting the speed loss from the gravitational gain leaves a net acceleration of thirty-eight microseconds every single day.

s06.text: Because radio signals travel at the speed of light, thirty-eight microseconds multiplies into eleven point four kilometers of positioning error every twenty-four hours.

s07.text: To fix this, engineers pre-slowed satellite atomic clocks before launch to ten point two two nine megahertz, so Einstein's universe makes them tick in perfect unison on Earth.
